Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the call this morning. Attached is our latest Order Form (v3) with redlines from procurement and a short note from legal on tax flow. High-level asks from Horizon: 

- We need net45 payment terms (Org policy).
- Horizon requests Redwood to accept VAT/GST withholding treatment where the reverse-charge does not apply — legal has flagged country-level withholding for certain entities and would like Redwood to absorb or provide an offset.
- Invoice routing: all invoices should go to procurement@horizon.health with PO reference in the subject; accounts payable prefers a single consolidated monthly invoice rather than multiple invoices per order line.
- We propose minimum commit schedule in Appendix A to be spread quarterly instead of front-loaded.

Can your finance/legal take a look and confirm what you can accept vs what needs escalation? We've also included a proposed signature block.

Attachments: Horizon_OrderForm_v3.pdf

Thanks,
Emily

Emily — thanks, got the redlines. Looping in Ben (AE) and Lauren (legal) and Karthik (finance ops) to triage. Quick read: 

1) Net terms — our standard is net30; we can approve net45 for enterprise deals with finance sign-off on ARR and credit checks. Ben, can you confirm expected ARR cadence if we agree to net45?

2) Taxes/withholding — Redwood’s position historically: customer is responsible for local withholding unless there's a specific negotiated credit in the order form. We can consider an invoicing offset for verified withholding taxes, but need evidence and a cap. Lauren — please advise on language to accept customer withholding with a gross-up or credit clause.

3) Invoice consolidation — Karthik, can we produce a consolidated monthly invoice for Horizon with PO in the subject and line-item breakout? Any limitations on prepaid tranches?

I’ll draft a short triage note for legal and finance so we can present options to Horizon by EOB Monday.

—Kimberly

Adding expected commercial context from our side so finance can size the risk: Horizon is targeting a 12-month adoption with a $720k committed minimum (quarterly tranches they want smoothed). If we accept net45 it increases DSO but it’s doable with a small credit holdback. My preference: accept net45 for the first 6 months as a concession, then revert to net30 on renewal; require upfront 25% deposit to cover first quarter commitments to protect cash.

Also — on minimum commits: Horizon’s ask to spread quarterly is fine but we should preserve annual commitment for expansion math. Lauren / Karthik — is a clause that ties invoicing cadence to the committed tranche (monthly consolidated invoice, but with line items showing tranche usage) acceptable operationally?

Hi all — thanks for the context. Quick legal triage below (high level — will provide redline suggestions in tracked PDF by EOB):

- Tax/withholding: We can accept customer withholding provided Horizon provides evidence of amount withheld and a government receipt; Redwood will provide a corresponding credit against future invoices equal to the documented withholding. We will not \"absorb\" withholding such that Redwood pays net taxes on Horizon’s behalf. Proposed clause: \"If Customer is required by applicable law to withhold taxes, Customer shall provide Redwood with official receipts; Redwood will issue a credit for such amounts against future invoices, subject to a maximum of X% per invoice unless otherwise agreed in writing.\"

- Gross-up: we will not gross-up pricing automatically. If Horizon requires gross-up, that would increase list pricing; Ben — please confirm if Horizon raised gross-up as a hard requirement.

- Net terms: we can accept net45 for this SOW on a pilot basis conditioned on (i) a 25% upfront payment, or (ii) an approved credit application and a signed acceptance of the staggered commitment schedule. If neither is acceptable, fallback is net30.

- Invoice consolidation: Operationally acceptable. Karthik — finance ops needs to confirm how we surface withholding as a credit on the consolidated invoice and whether we can attach the proof.

I will attach tracked language and two alternative Order Form signatures: one that preserves Redwood’s standard tax clause and one that accepts withholding with credit.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com

Emily / Emily’s team — operational confirmation from finance: 

- We can issue a single consolidated invoice monthly to procurement@horizon.health with PO in the subject and include a CSV of line items. Prepaid tranches: we will show the invoice credit balance and drawdown per tranche.
- Withholding credit: upon receipt of government withholding receipts (PDFs attached to the payment remittance), we will apply a credit in the next invoice cycle. We propose a rolling cap of 10% of the monthly invoice to avoid material cash mismatch; any out-of-band amounts above 10% should be escalated to finance ops for a manual review.
- Net terms: we are fine to pilot net45 if Horizon provides either the 25% upfront deposit or an approved credit application (we can start the credit review immediately if you share AP references).

Next steps: Lauren will send tracked redlines; Ben — please share the 25% deposit instruction (bank wiring vs ACH) and I’ll confirm invoice header requirements. Emily — can you send the PO template and any AP remittance instructions so we can mirror them on our invoices?

Thanks — Karthik
